verdicts.quote: “Using OAuth 2.0 is necessary for developing apps that are available in the Pipedrive Marketplace.”
verdicts.reason: Pipedrive supports both API tokens and OAuth, but for multi-tenant apps the docs make OAuth2 the intended method, so OAuth2 is the primary_auth.

verdicts.quote: “You’ll automatically be brought to the second tab, ‘OAuth & access scopes’, where you’ll get your client_id and client_secret.”
verdicts.reason: Devs can self‑serve a developer sandbox and then generate OAuth credentials in Developer Hub without needing a paid plan, so access is self_serve_free.

verdicts.quote: “Pipedrive’s API and extension points cover the majority of our core product’s functionality.”
verdicts.reason: The reference lists many resources (deals, persons, organizations, activities, products, pipelines, users, webhooks, etc.), indicating a broad API.

verdicts.quote: “Secure, self-hosted MCP server for Pipedrive CRM with v2 read tools, optional preview-first writes, stdio/HTTP transports, and Docker support.”
verdicts.reason: There is no vendor‑maintained MCP server in Pipedrive’s docs/GitHub, but multiple third‑party/community MCP servers exist, so mcp = community.

verdicts.quote: “Private apps can be shared with any user/company in Pipedrive via a direct, unlisted installation link. They don’t have to go through the app approval process and will not be published in the Pipedrive Marketplace.”
verdicts.reason: You can build and ship now using private apps and OAuth creds, but broader/public distribution requires Marketplace approval; hence ready_with_caveats.
